memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "We saw the Nephilim there (the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim). We seemed like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and we looked the same to them." — Num 13:33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the heart of the whole tragedy, and it lies in one revealing phrase: "We seemed like grasshoppers in our own eyes." Their defeat happened on the inside long before any battle was fought. They had already lost — not because the giants were too big, but because they had shrunk themselves down to grasshoppers.

Notice the second half: "and we looked the same to them." But how could they possibly know how they looked in the giants' eyes? They didn't. They were projecting their own fear onto their enemies, assuming everyone saw them as small as they saw themselves. Fear does this. It tells us not only that we are helpless, but that everyone else can see our helplessness too.

The root problem was that they measured themselves against the giants instead of measuring the giants against God. Compared to the Nephilim, of course they felt like grasshoppers. But they were never meant to face the giants in their own strength. The living God was on their side. Next to Him, the giants themselves were grasshoppers.

How we see ourselves shapes how we live. If we measure ourselves against our problems, we will always feel like grasshoppers. But if we remember whose we are — children of the Almighty God, indwelt by His Spirit — the picture changes entirely. In Christ we are not grasshoppers cowering before giants; we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us. Do not let fear write your identity. Let God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you see yourself as a grasshopper, or as a child of the Almighty God?
2. How does measuring yourself against problems instead of against God distort your view?
3. What would change if you truly believed you are "more than a conqueror" in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the times I have shrunk myself down to a grasshopper and forgotten who I am in You. Remind me that You are with me and greater than every giant. Let my identity rest in Christ, not in my fears. Amen.
